newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: One prisoner killed as guards quell Colombian riot.
newsitem.headline: One prisoner killed as guards quell Colombian riot.

text.p: At least one inmate was killed and another was seriously injured on Tuesday as guards moved to put down one of several riots that have rocked Colombia's overcrowded prison system in the past week, authorities said.

An official at the National Prisons Institute said the unidentified inmate was apparently caught in crossfire and killed as prison guards backed by reinforcements moved to quell a two-day-old uprising in the Modelo prison in Bucaramanga, capital of northern Santander province.
The prison official said he was also unable to identify the injured prisoner, also hit by gunshots.

Prisoners, some of them brandishing firearms and others wielding Molotov cocktails and rocks, fought pitched battles with guards for more than two hours before authorities claimed to have regained control over the facility late on Tuesday.
The Modelo prison houses some 1,200 inmates, many of them accused leftist guerrillas, and the riot there was the third in the past 1-1/2 months.
Provincial Gov. Mario Camacho said the riot at Modelo was staged as a "smokescreen" to cover up a planned mass breakout through a tunnel discovered by prison guards.
"The guards have finally managed to restore order," he said.

Police and penal authorities said another riot began on Tuesday in a penitentiary known as La Union in southwest Narino province where a group of more than 50 inmates was holding three guards hostage to press for better living conditions and the naming of a new warden.
Some inmates hurled rocks and other debris at police and soliders who cordoned off the facility after the riot erupted early on Tuesday but there were no reports of serious violence.

A tense standoff continued, meanwhile, at the main jail in Valledupar, capital of northern Cesar province, where an uprising by more than 580 prisoners has been under way since four guards were shot and killed inside the facility last Thursday.
Hundreds of security force members, backed by two light tanks, have ringed the prison -- which was built to hold no more than 150 inmates -- since the riot began.

Government officials have insisted that little progress can be made in the talks aimed at bringing the Valledupar uprising to a peaceful end unless the inmates, said to be led by a group of 10 men headed by a suspected leftist guerrilla, release 15 hostages and surrender the weapons they seized from prison guards.

At least 10 Colombian prisons have been torn by riots over the past two months to protest against poor living conditions and chronic overcrowding. Colombia's prison system was designed to hold a total of 30,000 inmates nationwide but authorities say 40,000 people are currently serving time behind bars.
